chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: Feather as a writer and the planned book chapter
summary: Hodes calls Feather a good craftsman but says his motives are suspect. He wants the jazz war included in the book.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Now, Leonard Feather is a very good writer, in my estimation, a good craftsman.
What did you say, he's a good craftsman?
Yeah, from where I set, I read him and I have to say, well, man, he writes good. It's what he says
or doesn't say where I'm suspect. But his writing, I can't say that -- and the --
But you suspect his motives because of what you know of his history.
And the amount of work he's --
And I never know what connection he's got with the artist he's writing about.
And the amount of work he puts out.
Well, he's a very fast writer. He will sit down at the typewriter and it'll just comes out.

Who else put out a Who's Who on jazz? Year after year, and things like that. To a certain extent, a lot of that is important, because if he doesn't hate you, you might get a lot of factual stuff there. At least, I don't know who else is doing it.

That's what I mean. That I don't want to put him down. But I'd just as soon let him rest, except that we are putting out a book and the story of the jazz war will be in there. If I have to take the book to a country publisher.
Yeah, I've talked to Leonard about that period, and I've always had the impression that he'd rather not talk about it, that it really wasn't as bad as everybody makes it out, and -- I love Art Hodes.
